review_text: I am generally happy with my new Norelco 7180XL, it is nice to have a new shaver, it is amazingly quiet, and gives a close and quick shave. But I feel that Norelco needs to improve both their instruction manual, and their customer support. Neither of these were in tune with my first experience with the 7180XL, as far as initial charging, and what the green charging light and red low battery light were doing. The manual calls for a 12 hour initial charge before using the shaver. When fully charged, the green light is supposed to blink. Well, on my initial charge, the light started blinking after 30 minutes. I did continue the charge for 12 hours anyway, the green light blinking the whole time. I called Norelco support, and was informed the manual was not correct, and that I had not damaged my shaver by completing the 12 hour charge. But no further explanation. Then I started using the shaver, and after just 2 shaves, the red low battery light came on. I went back to the Norelco website, and found a page on charging that said if the shaver did that, you should use it until the motor stops. They omit the obvious next step of charging it in these instructions, but say you will have no problem with the red light coming on too soon after following their directions. Well, I have done that, and it remains to be seen if my new Norelco will eventually sort itself out and work right. I must say I have my doubts after this initial experience, that it will last as long as my 7 year old model 5841XL did. I've used Norelco shavers for about 40 years, and never had any problems like this.
title: Will it outperform my 7 year old Norelco?

review_text: I have had schick--braun & panasonic foil razors.They all did a decent job but all left long hairs.The 7180 shaves clean-no long hairs left.It is very quiet & a close shave--holds charge for 7 shaves.I am 75 years old & shave daily.This is the best razor I've had to date & recommend it--makes shaving fun

review_text: I've been a wet shaver (safety razor, soap, and brush) for many years, but decided to try an electric to save time in the morning. I bought some Williams Lectric Shave and researched electric shaving technique online. After being disappointed by a foil, I settled on the 7180XL. It's a good mid-level razor at a reasonable price, balancing quietness, speed, ergonomics, and the necessary features. Unfortunately, it was too much of a step down from a proper wet shave. I didn't like: - the lack of precision (three cutting disks on a planar surface the size of my cheek) - it missed a lot of hairs, requiring several passes for a clean shave - although I used a light touch, pushing the shaver through the stubble was still irritating - the shave was socially acceptable in appearance, but rough to the touch - I had a 5 o'clock shadow by 2 o'clock - you can't do a close multi-pass shave for special occasions like you can with a blade - I started getting ingrown hairs on my neck Regarding the last point above, you really can't address that by using a blade on just special occasions. The face needs time to adjust to a change in shaving method, so if you switch between methods neither will be optimal. The 7180XL is a perfectly good razor for men who are satisfied with a socially acceptable shave and whose face can tolerate the rotary shaving system. It just wasn't my cup of tea. I now wet shave at night and still have less of a shadow by 5 o'clock than I would using an electric shaver in the morning.
title: Good electric razor, but doesn't compare to a proper wet shave

review_text: I have had these long enough to test all three colors. I'm satisfied these are clearly NOT frost. If you apply correctly, the mirror effect is better than the powders. However, the gold is more of a gold/green, not a true gold. The silver & rose gold are beautiful. To apply correctly and have the mirror effect, you must adhere to nail tech guidelines!! 1. Wash & scrub your nails with a nail brush. 2. Dry your nails! 3. Apply a base coat. This is VERY important to have a filled in base on your nails. I use Mia's. 4. Apply one thin coat to each nail. 5. Use a nail corrector pen or small brush dipped in acetone to remove any on cuticles. 6. Go back to first nail painted and apply a second, thicker coat. Repeat on other nails. 7. Repeat step 5. 8. Apply your choice of top coat. I use Mia's in my salon. If you can't get the same results, you're either not putting a base and top coat on or you're using too much on your first coat. Enjoy!!

review_text: I bought this because I was wanting to try fiberglass without spending a ton on something I might hate. I definitely do not hate these nails! They are a bit of a pain to use, and some of that pain is actual, physical pain from getting fiberglass stuck in your skin. I'd advise using gloves, and will follow my own advice on that going forward. Fiberglass is actual wee little glass fibers which are nearly impossible to see and remove when you get a bit stuck in your skin and can be really irritating and painful. I ended up smearing my hands with tacky glue, letting it dry, and then peeling it off to get rid of the it. It worked pretty well, but yeah, gloves. The gel in this set cured well, and as I said, my nails are very strong. I used Young Nails Protien Bond and the base coat, and so far no lifting whatsoever, when I usually would start seeing some. The little LED light is cute, but I wouldn't ever use it for curing nails. I have a better light and I halved the recommending curing times since they're given for the tiny lamp. The little side set of a cuticle pusher and nail files was nice, I really enjoyed the addition of a cuticle trimmer. The powders are absolutely amazing. These are the first powders I've ever used that came out perfect, nail after nail. It was extremely easy, and the powder so smoothly covered the nail that I didn't even need to buff them before top coat. They were just smooth, I've never had that happen with dip powders before. The color is also nice and vibrant, you don't need more than 3 dips (I wanted a nice, solid pink) to achieve your look. The addition of the brush saver (step 4) was a lifesaver, I feel it's a must have for doing dip nails. I didn't like the top coat at all. It didn't spread well, felt stiff, didn't give a good shine... it didn't make sense as the rest of the kit was pretty great. I'd use another top coat next time. Also, the pots of powder are kind of small to dip your nails in, but I made it work. I'd definitely purchase the powders again, I would love to see a powder and brush saver set! Also, there is no pickup tube that goes to the bottom, so you have to keep whacking the top against your hand, as if you’re packing a new box of smokes, or it’ll run dry. There is no smell, or at least neither one of us could smell anything at all. It’s very creamy (white), and absorbs into her skin quickly. There is a moist, tacky feeling to the skin for a few minutes, and then it’s gone. So you have to wait a few minutes after application to apply makeup. She has pretty sensitive skin, and said there was no redness or tightness, or any adverse reaction at all. Too early to tell if it reduces wrinkles, but as far as anti-aging goes, she wore this cream for about a week, and her birthday still came. Hope this helps.
